name: May 26, 2026 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
Minutes
  Lakewood City Council
  Regular Meeting held
  May 26, 2026

MEETING WAS CALLED TO ORDER at 7:32 p.m. by Mayor Chase in the Council Chambers at
the Civic Center, 5000 Clark Avenue, Lakewood, California.

INVOCATION was offered by Pastor Candace Kelly, Acts Community Bible Church

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE was led by Scouting America Cub Scout Pack 247

ROLL CALL: PRESENT: Mayor Cassandra Chase
  Vice Mayor Jeff Wood
  Council Member David Arellano
  Council Member Steve Croft
  Council Member Todd Rogers
  .  .  .

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS:

Mayor Chase 1) announced that the meeting would be adjourned in memory of a) former
Maintenance Carpenter Ted Pflug; and b) the victims of the Islamic Center of San Diego;
2) highlighted the Memorial Day Commemoration held on May 25, 2026, at the
Lakewood Veterans Memorial Plaza at Del Valle Park; and 3) declared May 2026 as a) Asian
American and Pacific Islander Heritage month, highlighting that Asian Americans and Pacific
Islanders make up about 15% of Lakewood’s population; and b) Mental Health Awareness
month, further noting that the City contracts with Care Solace to help residents connect with
mental health and substance use resources.

Vice Mayor Wood 1) sent his condolences to those affected by the Garden Grove chemical
leak; 2) reported on his attendance at the a) California Contract Cities Association Annual
Municipal Webinar, noting that he was asked to serve on the Executive Board; b) Public Works
Week Event; c) Chick-fil-A grand reopening; and d) Memorial Day Commemoration; and
3) requested staff contact the City of Long Beach regarding bike share bicycles that are
abandoned in the City.

Council Member Rogers 1) provided a verbal report of the crime trends and statistics from the
Public Safety Committee; 2) explained that the City must follow the State of California’s
mandates relative to Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs), noting that the City cannot deny an
ADU permit if it meets Statewide requirements; 3) requested an update relative to the
Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) installations; and 4) encouraged residents to
report warning signs of an active shooter.

At the request of Council Member Rogers, Director of Public Safety Yordt confirmed that the
1) Flock ALPRs are scheduled to be removed; and 2) Motorola Vigilant ALPRs will ship
within the next few weeks.

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS - Continued

Council Member Arellano 1) reported on his attendance at the a) ICSC Las Vegas Conference;
and b) Silver Award Ceremony held at Lakewood High School, further congratulating the
Girl Scouts of Greater Los Angeles for their hard work and dedication; and 2) expressed
gratitude for serving as a member of the City Council.

At the request of Council Member Arellano, Director of Community Development Cervantes
provided a brief verbal report of the meetings and discussions held during the ICSC Las Vegas
Conference.

For the record, Mayor Chase introduced Eddie Witt Jr., Chair of Lemonade Day, and
Jesse Gilgoff, Vice President of the Lakewood Jaycees, who provided a verbal report on
Lemonade Day.
  .  .  .

PUBLIC COMMENT ON ITEMS IN THE AGENDA - None
  .  .  .

ROUTINE ITEMS:

It was moved by Council Member Arellano, seconded by Council Member Rogers, and carried
unanimously by the following roll call vote, to approve the balance of the actions stipulated on
the Routine Items:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase

RI-1 Approval of Minutes of the Meeting held May 12, 2026

RI-2 Approval of Personnel Transactions

RI-3 Approval of Registers of Demands

RI-4 Approval of City Council Committees’ Activities

RI-5 Approval of Meeting Reports and Authorizations Pursuant to AB1234

RI-7 Approval of Resolution No. 2026-14 - Consenting to the Inclusion of Properties within

  Assessed Clean Energy Programs; Authorizing the California Statewide Communities

  Contractual Assessment Proceedings and Levy Contractual Assessments within the City;
  and Authorizing Related Actions

3.1 • SUMMER PROGRAMS, CIVIC CENTER BLOCK PARTY AND RECREATION
CATALOG PREVIEW

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Director of Recreation and Community Services Frost provided a PowerPoint presentation of
the Agenda report.

For the record, and without objection, the report was received and filed.
  .  .  .

3.2 • RESOLUTION NO. 2026-16 - ADOPTION OF A DISRUPTION OF
TELEPHONIC OR INTERNET SERVICE DURING MEETINGS POLICY IN
ACCORDANCE WITH SENATE BILL 707

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Deputy City Manager Beltran 1) provided a PowerPoint presentation of the Agenda report; and
2) along with City Manager McCormack and Deputy City Attorney Skolnik, responded to
Council Members’ questions.

At the request of Council Member Croft and Vice Mayor Wood, 1) Deputy City Manager
Beltran confirmed that Senate Bill 707 does not apply to the State Senate and/or
State Assembly; and 2) City Manager McCormack explained that if telephonic or internet
service is not operational at the meeting location, the City Council is not required to provide
remote access; however, the City would make a good-faith attempt to establish telephonic or
internet connection for remote participation.

In response to questions and comments provided by Council Member Rogers and
Council Member Arellano, 1) Deputy City Manager Beltran a) clarified that in the event of
disruption of telephonic and/or internet service, the City must call for a recess of the open
session for at least one hour following the disruption, or until the service is restored, whichever
is earlier; and b) confirmed that staff can look into supplemental technology systems that can
be used in the event of a service disruption of the main system; and 2) Deputy City Attorney
Skolnik clarified that remote access applies to all open and public meetings of the City Council
as required by the Ralph M. Brown Act.

Following discussion, it was moved by Vice Mayor Wood, seconded by
Council Member Arellano, and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to adopt
Resolution No. 2026-16:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase
  .  .  .

LAKEWOOD HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY

1 • REGISTER OF DEMANDS

It was moved by Council Member Rogers, seconded by Council Member Arellano, and
unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to approve the register of demands:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase
  .  .  .

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

Ben Chavez, resident, 1) thanked the City Council for the Memorial Day Commemoration
held at the Lakewood Veterans Memorial Plaza; 2) highlighted that with the recent street
marking on the south side of Centralia Street, residents have been able to walk safely in the
area; and 3) requested the City look into conducting a parking study in the vicinity of 215 th
Street and Nectar Avenue, further explaining that individuals regularly park their vehicles
within fifteen feet of the intersection which causes safety concerns.

Philip Norris, resident, 1) suggested the City consider a) utilizing Los Angeles County
Sheriff’s Search Dogs for drug enforcement; b) relative to Ordinance No. 2026-1, requiring
wider parking spaces at an angle to accommodate larger vehicles; c) utilizing Orange County
Transportation Authority or Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority for
transportation services, expressing the opinion that very few residents utilize Long Beach
Transit within the City; d) strict enforcement of not allowing parking within one hundred feet
of a driveway; and e) reconfiguring the lanes on Harvey Way, Pioneer Boulevard, and
Centralia Street, similar to the lane reconfiguration recently completed on Palo Verde Avenue;
and 2) requested an update on the Palms Park Community Center Improvements Project.

Tom Swanner, resident, expressed concerns relative to an active code enforcement case at
5902 Premiere Avenue, stating 1) the existing “granny flat” has been in existence since 1951;
2) the subject property was reassessed with the “granny flat” by the County of Los Angeles;
3) the “granny flat” has been memorialized with plot maps and setbacks; and 4) an amicable
resolution has not yet been found.

May 26, 2026

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - Continued

In response to the comments provided by Tom Swanner, Mayor Chase 1) stated that this is an
active code enforcement investigation; and 2) suggested he speak with Director of Community
Development Cervantes.

David Olson, expressed concerns relative to an active code enforcement case at 5902 Premiere
Avenue, stating 1) as a contractor and former City of Arcadia Planning Commissioner, he is
well versed in zoning and building codes; and 2) he inspected the subject property and found
the structure in compliance with relative codes.

Hector Vargas, resident, expressed concerns relative to an active code enforcement case at
5902 Premiere Avenue, stating 1) his in-laws reside with him and the subject property due to
health issues; 2) the City inspected the property and noted that it is “permit exempt as used”;
however, the City later described the property as “dilapidated” and “improperly maintained”;
3) he met with Code Enforcement Manager Carter relative to the Notice to Abate received but
there has yet to be a resolution; and 4) the process has raised a “broader concern” on how code
enforcement matters are being handled in the City.

In response to the comments provided by Hector Vargas, Mayor Chase suggested he speak
with Director of Community Development Cervantes.
  .  .  .

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business to be brought before the City Council, Mayor Chase adjourned
the meeting at 8:49 p.m. to Tuesday, June 9, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in the Executive Board Room.
A moment of silence was observed in memory of Ted Pflug and the victims of the Islamic
Center of San Diego.

Respectfully submitted,

Dakota Wallace, CMC
City Clerk
